extraction.name: ArtifactsBench
extraction.description: ArtifactsBench is a benchmark for evaluating LLMs on interactive visual artifacts. It contains 1,825 executable queries across nine domains and uses an automated multimodal evaluation pipeline that executes artifacts in a sandbox, captures three staged screenshots, and scores outputs with checklist-guided MLLM referees.
extraction.creator: Tencent Hunyuan Team
extraction.citeAs: ArtifactsBench: Bridging the Visual-Interactive Gap in LLM Code Generation Evaluation
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The benchmark was curated through a multi-stage pipeline combining expert sourcing with LLM generation and refinement. Candidates were aggregated from expert showcases, open SVG/web-snippet datasets, web case studies, and LLM visual-to-query from screenshots. Automated filters removed incomplete, non-visual, license-violating, duplicate, trivial, or non-interactive items. Experts rewrote prompts for clarity, completeness, and executability; LLM rewriting added diverse styles; humans verified the results. De-duplication and contamination control used MinHash and semantic similarity over prompts, checklists, and normalized DOM/CSS/JS, plus screenshot perceptual hashing. Tasks solved only by brittle hacks were revised or removed. Difficulty was assigned post hoc by aggregated performance of 30+ LLMs.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Software Collection, Secondary Data analysis, Document analysis, Others
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Candidate tasks were sourced from expert showcases, open SVG/web-snippet datasets, web case studies, and LLM visual-to-query generated from screenshots.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Automated filters dropped incomplete, non-visual, license-violating, duplicate, trivial, or non-interactive items. Two-stage de-duplication and contamination control used MinHash plus semantic similarity over prompts, checklists, and normalized DOM/CSS/JS, followed by screenshot perceptual hashing. Flagged items were re-authored or discarded. Experts rewrote prompts, LLMs rewrote for style diversity, humans verified them, and tasks solved only by brittle hacks were revised or removed. Difficulty labels were assigned post hoc by aggregated performance of 30+ models, and sub-categories were tagged by a lightweight classifier with human spot-checks.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The pipeline standardized execution with headless Chromium via Playwright at 1024×768 resolution and deterministic seeds. Three staged screenshots were captured before, during, and after scripted interaction. Prompts and checklists were prepared to emphasize executable code and observable interaction, while purely static items were retained when visual fidelity or structured graphics were primary goals.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Each query was paired with a 10-dimension checklist covering visual, interactional, and code qualities. Checklists were drafted by Hunyuan-Turbos and then human-refined for specificity and screenability. A 10% manually curated seed anchored calibration and was reused as few-shot references to keep difficulty high and rubrics consistent. Human validation was conducted on 280 queries and 6 models in a double-blind study scored by multiple front-end engineers; the final human ground-truth score was the median of individual annotators' ratings.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Checklist calibration achieved Cohen's kappa >= 0.8 among annotators on the 10% manually curated seed. In the human validation study, agreement between automated referees and human experts was measured by Pair ACC, defined over pairwise ranking consistency. The final human ground-truth score was the median of individual annotators' ratings. The paper also analyzes cross-judge ranking consistency between Gemini-2.5-Pro and Qwen2.5-VL-72B and reports version stability for Gemini.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Multiple engineers with extensive front-end development experience; front-end engineers; annotators in the checklist calibration study.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The benchmark, evaluation harness, and baseline results are open sourced at https://artifactsbenchmark.github.io. The paper states release of dataset specs, checklist templates, evaluation scripts, and referee settings. It discusses version stability by replacing deprecated Gemini-2.5-Pro-Preview-0506 with stable Gemini-2.5-Pro without changing conclusions, but no explicit update timeframe or deprecation policy for the dataset itself is provided.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The query quality filtering prompt explicitly includes a Privacy dimension requiring that questions avoid sensitive personal information such as phone numbers, addresses, or other identifiable details.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark is intended to provide the community with a scalable and accurate tool to accelerate the development of user-centric generative models. The paper argues that high-fidelity, functional interactive visual artifacts are central to user experience in modern applications and that their quality directly affects real-world adoption.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The paper notes that multimodal LLM referees can suffer from hallucination, prompt sensitivity, limited awareness of engineering/code quality, version drift, and potential cognitive biases in interpreting long-horizon interaction logic and dynamic visual feedback. It also notes that referee evaluation criteria may diverge from human judgments because referees can extract additional strengths and weaknesses from the code-level perspective.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The current methodology evaluates dynamic behavior using a sequence of screenshots at fixed intervals, which may not fully capture highly complex, long-horizon, or state-dependent interactions such as multi-step user workflows or nuanced game physics. The benchmark focuses on the final artifact generated in a single turn and does not assess iterative agentic refinement, self-debugging, or multi-turn development processes.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is used as a benchmark for evaluating LLMs on interactive visual artifact generation. It supports automated, holistic, and reproducible evaluation of code, visuals, and interaction across 1,825 tasks, fine-grained capability analysis across domains and difficulty tiers, leaderboard comparison of 30+ models, human-alignment validation, and diagnostic analysis of strengths and failure modes.
